points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the existing candidate record and were not re-adjudicated.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English Google result pages. Page one mixes Google Cloud overview, how-to, CLI reference, blog, forum, one video, codelab, Medium, and an independent monitoring article; page two drops into generic Cloud Run FAQs, forums, networking videos, vendor integrations, and unrelated endpoint material.

G2=pass: implementation-oriented inner pages, forums, and independent articles occupy substantial space; there is no video, wiki, major-media, or strong-brand-homepage takeover, and page two establishes a clear relevance cliff.

The Google Cloud Create and run Connectivity Tests guide has an exact section for testing from a Cloud Run job to a VM instance or another supported endpoint, providing the task workflow and appearing as the second natural result.

The separately indexed gcloud connectivity-tests update reference provides a second free executable path: it documents the test identifier and the --source-cloud-run-job=SOURCE_CLOUD_RUN_JOB flag, including clearing or replacing the Cloud Run job URI source endpoint.

G3=veto: two free exact-task completion pages are already stably visible on page one—the complete how-to and the executable CLI reference. Overview, blog, forum, and general Cloud Run pages are not counted.
This is not veto_window_bet because both task-completing pages are already indexed and visible; there is no temporary unindexed gap.
Caveat: Chrome used a signed-in Google session with gl=us, hl=en, pws=0; the result footer reported that results were not personalized, while safe=active and ssui=on were appended by Google.
